Case Studies / JDK Factory ERP

JDK Factory ERP

Case study · Manufacturing

An ERP built around how a cement plant actually works, delivered in 30 days.

JDK is a cement manufacturer. Its team had been using Odoo, but found it unnecessarily complicated and rigid for day-to-day operations. We replaced it with a simpler system built around the plant's own workflow.

Sector
Cement manufacturing
Replaced
Odoo
Time to delivery
30 days
Platform
React front end, FastAPI back end

The challenge

A general-purpose ERP has to serve every kind of business, and JDK was paying for that generality in complexity. Everyday tasks took too many steps, and processes specific to cement production had to be bent to fit the software rather than the other way round. The team wanted a system that was straightforward to use and ready for where the business was heading.

The approach

We mapped the plant's operational workflow first — how a customer order becomes a production requirement, how materials are sourced and received, and how finished output is bagged, batched and delivered. The core workflows were then rebuilt around those processes, so the system reflects how JDK operates rather than a generic template.

The solution: one connected workflow

  1. Sales
  2. Feasibility
  3. Quotation
  4. Order
  5. Procurement
  6. Inventory
  7. Production
  8. Delivery
  9. Payment
  • Sales, procurement and production connected — a customer order, the materials needed to fulfil it and the output ready to leave the plant sit in one record, with no re-keying between departments.
  • Built for cement operations — bagging, batches and inventory movements are first-class parts of the system.
  • Role-based access — each team sees its own tasks, while leadership sees the whole operation.
  • A modern web stack — React on the front end and FastAPI on the back end, faster to use and easier to extend.

The outcome

The system was delivered in 30 days as a clear step forward from the previous tool.

  • Less re-keying — information is entered once and reused across sales, inventory and production.
  • Visibility for managers — what has been ordered, what is in production and what is ready for delivery is visible in one place.
  • A system that fits the plant — it follows real cement operations rather than forcing workarounds.
  • Usable anywhere on site — it runs in the browser, in the office, on the plant floor or on a tablet.

What it demonstrates

  • Replacing a generic package with business-specific software
  • Understanding a manufacturing workflow end to end before building
  • One shared record of each order in place of hand-offs between tools
  • Enterprise software delivered on a 30-day timeline
